components.css: :host{--ground:#121110;--ground-2:#1c1a17;--rule:#3b3732;--rule-strong:#5c564d;--text:#f4efe3;--muted:#b8b0a1;--paper:#f4efe3;--paper-ink:#1a1714;--paper-muted:#574f45;--red:#c8202f;--red-down:#a51a26;--mustard:#f2b21b;--d1960:#1f4fa8;--d1990:#1c8c6e;--key:'League Gothic','Barlow Condensed',sans-serif;--label:'Barlow Condensed','Barlow',sans-serif;--body:'Barlow',system-ui,sans-serif;--ease-out:cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);} .ds-rack{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;background:var(--ground);padding:12px;} .ds-strip{display:grid;grid-template-columns:4.6rem 1fr;grid-template-rows:auto auto;column-gap:12px;align-items:center;background:var(--paper);color:var(--paper-ink);border-top:7px solid var(--deck,var(--mustard));padding:8px 14px 9px 12px;min-height:66px;} .ds-year{grid-row:1/3;font-family:var(--key);font-size:2.5rem;line-height:1;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;} .ds-title{font-family:var(--label);font-weight:700;font-size:1.12rem;line-height:1.15;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.01em;} .ds-artist{font-family:var(--body);font-size:0.92rem;line-height:1.25;color:var(--paper-muted);} .ds-mystery{border-top-color:var(--mustard);background:var(--ground-2);color:var(--text);border-left:1px dashed var(--rule-strong);border-right:1px dashed var(--rule-strong);border-bottom:1px dashed var(--rule-strong);} .ds-mystery .ds-year{color:var(--mustard);} .ds-mystery .ds-artist{color:var(--muted);} .ds-slot{height:50px;background:var(--ground-2);border:1px solid var(--rule);border-top:7px solid var(--rule-strong);color:var(--text);font-family:var(--label);font-weight:700;font-size:1rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.05em;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 120ms,color 120ms,border-color 120ms;} .ds-slot:hover{background:var(--mustard);border-color:var(--mustard);color:var(--paper-ink);} .ds-slot:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--mustard);outline-offset:3px;}

narrative.overview:
Every song in ChronoSono is a printed paper title strip: cream stock, a flat band of ink across the top that names its decade, and the year set large in a condensed gothic as the selection key. A team's timeline is a rack of these strips stacked on black lacquer. The hidden song is the one strip still face down, a dark dashed blank with a mustard band and a question mark, and the reveal turns it over like a page in the rack.

The system is built for a dim living room and an arm's-length read. Contrast is high, type is tall and condensed, tap targets start at 40px and the important ones are 48px to 60px. Chrome is quiet: white-on-black labels, one-pixel rules between sections, lists that read as ruled ledgers rather than stacked cards. Color lives on paper (the decade bands) and in two signals: red for the brand and the main action, mustard for "this one, now."

Two things move: the logo on the home screen and the reveal flip. Everything else changes state in 120ms or less, and reduced motion stops all of it.
keyCharacteristics: Black lacquer ground, cream paper strips, ink type on paper.
One flat colored top band per decade, eight decades, never a gradient.
League Gothic for years, codes, counts, and short commands; Barlow Condensed uppercase for labels; Barlow for sentences.
Square surfaces; a 2px corner only on tappable controls.
Depth by tone (ground, raised ground, paper), separated by one-pixel rules.
A morphing logo: a clock running backward carried through record, cassette, CD, iPod, and app tile.

rules.name: The Decade Ink Rule
rules.body: Decade color appears only as the flat top band of a paper strip, and every band sits beside its year in type. Color is never the only cue for a decade.

rules.name: The Mustard Means Now Rule
rules.body: Mustard marks the one selected, current, or focused thing on screen. If nothing is selected, there is no mustard.

rules.name: The Red Is the Brand Rule
rules.body: Red marks the brand (logo, room code) and the single primary action in a view. It is not used for errors; errors use bad.

rules.name: The Gothic Key Rule
rules.body: League Gothic is for numbers, codes, names of the moment, and commands of a few words. It never sets a sentence.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or lines up (years, codes, counts, scores, the countdown) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Flat Rack Rule
rules.body: Strips, panels, buttons, and cells sit flat on the ground. Separation comes from tone and hairlines, never from shadows or glows.

dos: **Do** put every song on a paper strip with its decade band on top and its year in League Gothic beside it.
**Do** keep decade color to the band; the year in type is the cue that does not rely on color.
**Do** use mustard for exactly what is selected, current, or focused, and red for the brand and the one primary action.
**Do** separate sections and list rows with one-pixel rules on the open ground instead of boxing them.
**Do** keep tap targets at 48px or more for anything used mid-game (40px only for small secondary buttons).
**Do** use tabular figures for every number that changes.
**Do** keep motion to the logo and the reveal, with state transitions at 120ms, and honor reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** round surfaces; strips, panels, banners, and cells stay square, and controls stop at 2px.
**Don't** use glows or soft gradients. Hard-stop gradients that draw a crisp line (the dial handles) are fine.
**Don't** add shadows to strips, panels, or buttons; the toast is the only lifted element.
**Don't** set sentences in League Gothic or in uppercase.
**Don't** show a song title, artist, or year before the reveal; the mystery strip is the only representation of the current song.
**Don't** use real brand logos in the mark or anywhere else.
